previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia s/p stem cell transplant, multiple compression fractures, and recent cardiogenic shock was admitted for septic shock with fever, chills, and dyspnea. She was treated in the ICU with vasopressors and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to ceftriaxone for a likely urinary source. Imaging revealed right gluteal myositis, confirmed by ultrasound, and no abscess. She developed transient toxic-metabolic encephalopathy after physical therapy, prompting discontinuation of ropinirole due to suspected adverse effects. Her liver enzymes, initially elevated, improved with stabilization. She was transitioned to the floor, completed a seven-day IV antibiotic course, and was discharged to rehabilitation with plans for anticoagulation follow-up, neurology evaluation, and ongoing management of GVHD and diabetes.

is admitted from clinic because of a leg wound that had not been 
improving with antibiotics as well as new diarrhea. 

#LLE wound:
She was started on vancomycin on admission, but it was stopped 
on hospital day 2 as the wound did not appear infected. The 
wound was most likely persistent because of necrotic tissue that 
was presenting it from healing. Surgery did a bedside 
debridement, and wound care gave recommendations for dressing 
the wound. She will follow up in wound care clinic. For pain 
control she was given PO Dilaudid. 

#Diarrhea: 
She was endorsing diarrhea in clinic, but by the time she 
reached the floor her diarrhea had resolved so C. diff was not 
sent. The patient thinks the diarrhea was due to the PO 
antibiotics because this has happened before. As her diarrhea 
resolved prior to arrival there were no changes made other than 
to continue holding antibiotics.

#Weight loss:
Her weight on admission was 135, which is ___ down from her 
baseline weight. She reports that for the past 2 weeks she had 
been having decreased appetite because of the diarrhea and 
attributes her weight loss to this. She also has a history of 
chronic diarrhea and nausea. On discharge she reported that her 
appetite had improved back to normal; however, this is still a 
significant amount of weight for her to lose in 2 weeks and 
should continue to be monitored as an outpatient.

#CML s/p Allo-SCT ___:
Her IgG was low at 397 so she was given 25g IVIg. She was 
continued on her home prophylaxis medications of acyclovir and 
fluconazole.

#GVHD:
Has involvement of eyes and mouth. She was continued on her home 
prednisone and eye drops. 

#Depression/anxiety:
Continued home venlafaxine and mirtazapine 

#DM:
A1C 6.1%. She was managed with HISS and glargine.

#History of DVT/PE
Continued home Lovenox 60mg Q12H.

Transitional Issues:
- Recent weight loss, please trend weight to make sure not still 
losing. she thinks her weight loss was due to diarrhea and 
decreased appetite from diarrhea caused by antibiotics
- Monitor wound for signs of infection/purulent drainage
- Gave her 20 pills of Dilaudid 2mg, she does not need to be
